resources.string: Flint uses Android Accessibility to detect which app is in the foreground using app and screen class names, and read web addresses from known browser address bars for website blocking. Not all browsers or pages expose an address. In the browsers Flint supports, while a website rule is active, Flint also re-reads the address bar when a page changes without opening a new tab. Android sends page-change signals from other apps too; Flint ignores those without reading their content. See the Known adapters browser list on the You health screen in Flint. Address-bar URLs stay on this device, in memory for blocking; they are not saved as browsing history. Websites you enter remain in your rules. Address-bar reading stops when Accessibility is off. You can turn this service off in Android Accessibility settings. This data is used only to enforce your blocks, stays on your device, and is never sent off your device, shared, or sold. No account or analytics.
